subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: For strict sanitizer mode, should an unclosed reasoning opener followed by a `<final>` boundary recover only the final answer, suppress the whole malformed payload, or preserve the current answer-recovery fallback?
rationale: The source-reproducible leak sits at a security boundary: recovering text from malformed model output can save the answer, but the current fallback can expose hidden reasoning to external chat recipients.

options.title: Recover final-only text
options.body: Treat a valid final opener after an unclosed reasoning tag as the visible-answer boundary, strip preceding reasoning, and require focused sanitizer plus channel-delivery tests before closing this issue.

options.title: Fail closed on malformed reasoning
options.body: Suppress the whole malformed payload when strict mode sees an unclosed reasoning tag, accepting possible empty replies to minimize reasoning exposure.

options.title: Keep current fallback
options.body: Rely on native Gemini mitigation and accept the remaining malformed-tag risk until stronger live evidence or a broader channel policy decision appears.

recommendation.title: Recover final-only text
recommendation.body: Treat a valid final opener after an unclosed reasoning tag as the visible-answer boundary, strip preceding reasoning, and require focused sanitizer plus channel-delivery tests before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared reasoning/final tag sanitizer history points to this person as the strongest routing candidate for the strict-mode fallback decision.
